claim: The adult mouse incisor grows continuously throughout the animal's life.
source: An emerging model for studying adult mammalian tissue renewal is the rodent incisor, which grows continuously throughout the animal's life.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction describing a fundamental characteristic of the rodent incisor.

claim: Ameloblasts and odontoblasts are constantly generated by progenitors located at the proximal end of the tooth.
source: A number of cell types, including the ameloblasts and odontoblasts that secrete the mineralized enamel and dentin, respectively, are constantly generated by progenitors located at the proximal end of the tooth (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: The manuscript directly states this and references Figure 1A,B as visual support.

claim: Stem cell progeny leave the labial cervical loop niche as they begin differentiation.
source: In the epithelial compartment, stem cell progeny leave the niche, known as the labial cervical loop (laCL), as they begin the process of differentiation, and they then enter a transit-amplifying (T-A) zone and proliferate (Kuang-Hsien Hu et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is directly made in the text with citation support.

claim: Transit-amplifying cells in the incisor epithelium proliferate after leaving the stem cell niche.
source: In the epithelial compartment, stem cell progeny leave the niche, known as the labial cervical loop (laCL), as they begin the process of differentiation, and they then enter a transit-amplifying (T-A) zone and proliferate (Kuang-Hsien Hu et al., 2014).
evidence: The text explicitly states that cells enter a T-A zone and proliferate, with citation support.

claim: Differentiated epithelial cells undergo apoptosis as they advance towards the distal tip of the incisor.
source: These cells then differentiate, secrete matrix, and finally undergo apoptosis, all the while gradually advancing towards the distal tip of the organ.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the fate of differentiated cells.

claim: The incisor exhibits a conveyor belt-like organization with cells at progressively more distal locations representing increasingly advanced stages of maturation.
source: This linearity, akin to a conveyor belt, makes the incisor a useful model system to study adult epithelial tissue homeostasis, as tissue renewal occurs in an easily-observed proximo-distal fashion, whereby cells at increasingly advanced stages of maturation are found at progressively more distal locations (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this spatial organization pattern with figure reference.

claim: The mesenchyme of the incisor has distinct compartments comprised of progenitors that give rise to various differentiated cell types.
source: The organization of the mesenchyme has been less well-studied than the epithelium, but this tissue also has distinct compartments comprised of progenitors that give rise to various differentiated cell types, including the dentin-producing odontoblasts (Feng et al., 2011; Kaukua et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is directly made with citation support.

claim: The periodontium wraps the incisor growth region and anchors the tooth in the jaw.
source: A tissue complex of mesenchymal origin known as the periodontium wraps the incisor growth region and anchors the tooth in the jaw (Nanci and Bosshardt, 2006).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Gli1 marks stem cell populations in both the incisor epithelium and mesenchyme.
source: In vivo lineage tracing assays have identified Gli1 and Bmi1-expressing populations of stem cells in both the incisor epithelium and mesenchyme (Biehs et al., 2013; Seidel et al., 2010).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with citation support.

claim: Bmi1 marks stem cell populations in both the incisor epithelium and mesenchyme.
source: In vivo lineage tracing assays have identified Gli1 and Bmi1-expressing populations of stem cells in both the incisor epithelium and mesenchyme (Biehs et al., 2013; Seidel et al., 2010).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with citation support.

claim: Gli1 and Bmi1 mark label-retaining cells that divide infrequently.
source: Both Gli1 and Bmi1 also mark label-retaining cells (LRCs) that divide infrequently and therefore retain BrdU or genetic labels.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the properties of cells marked by these genes.

claim: Label-retaining cells in the incisor are restricted to the proximal incisor mesenchyme and the proximal part of the labial and lingual cervical loops.
source: Within the incisor, LRCs are restricted to the proximal incisor mesenchyme and the proximal part of the laCL and lingual cervical loop (liCL).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the spatial distribution of LRCs.

claim: Sox2 is a stem cell marker in the incisor epithelium but not the mesenchyme.
source: Additional lineage-tracing studies identified Sox2 as a stem cell marker in the incisor epithelium but not the mesenchyme (Juuri et al., 2012).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with citation support.

claim: Only three markers (Gli1, Bmi1, and Sox2) have been found to label incisor stem cells prior to this study.
source: To date, only these three markers have been found to label incisor stem cells, and thus a major limitation of the incisor model has been a paucity of markers that clearly distinguish its cell types, including progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the state of knowledge prior to the study.

claim: Gene co-expression analysis is a powerful approach for elucidating transcriptional signatures of distinct cell types in heterogeneous tissue samples.
source: Gene co-expression analysis is a powerful approach for elucidating transcriptional signatures of distinct cell types in heterogeneous tissue samples (Oldham et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Different cell types express different genes.
source: This approach is based on two straightforward ideas: (i) different cell types express different genes, and (ii) the relative abundance of a given cell type will vary among heterogeneous tissue samples.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a foundational principle.

claim: The relative abundance of a given cell type will vary among heterogeneous tissue samples.
source: This approach is based on two straightforward ideas: (i) different cell types express different genes, and (ii) the relative abundance of a given cell type will vary among heterogeneous tissue samples.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a foundational principle.

claim: Transcript levels of genes specifically expressed by a cell type will appear highly correlated when measured over a large number of biological replicates.
source: Therefore, transcript levels of genes that are specifically and consistently expressed by a cell type will appear highly correlated when measured over a large number of biological replicates.
evidence: This is a direct logical statement about the basis of the co-expression approach.

claim: The study identified modules of co-expressed genes representing differentiated cells, transit-amplifying cells, and residents of stem cell niches.
source: We identified modules of co-expressed genes representing differentiated cells, transit-amplifying cells, and residents of stem cell niches.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the study's findings.

claim: Lrig1 defines a population of incisor epithelial stem cells.
source: Through in vivo lineage tracing, we demonstrated the power of this approach by showing that co-expression module members Lrig1 and Igfbp5 define populations of incisor epithelial and mesenchymal stem cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a key finding with experimental support.

claim: Igfbp5 defines a population of incisor mesenchymal stem cells.
source: Through in vivo lineage tracing, we demonstrated the power of this approach by showing that co-expression module members Lrig1 and Igfbp5 define populations of incisor epithelial and mesenchymal stem cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a key finding with experimental support.

claim: The periodontium and dental pulp are maintained by distinct pools of stem cells.
source: We further discovered that two adjacent mesenchymal tissues, the periodontium and dental pulp, are maintained by distinct pools of stem cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a major discovery.

claim: Proximal incisor samples were micro-dissected from 94 six-week-old female CD1 wild-type mice.
source: We micro-dissected proximal incisor samples from 94 six-week-old female CD1 wild-type mice; each tissue sample was heterogeneous and consisted of the entire range of cell types present in the proximal incisor region (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental methodology.

claim: Each tissue sample was heterogeneous and consisted of the entire range of cell types present in the proximal incisor region.
source: We micro-dissected proximal incisor samples from 94 six-week-old female CD1 wild-type mice; each tissue sample was heterogeneous and consisted of the entire range of cell types present in the proximal incisor region (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the nature of the samples.

claim: Transcriptomes were profiled using Illumina Mouse Ref 8 v2.0 gene expression BeadChip microarrays containing 25,697 probes.
source: We profiled transcriptomes using Illumina Mouse Ref 8 v2.0 gene expression BeadChip microarrays, which contain 25,697 probes.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental methodology.

claim: 24 modules of co-expressed genes were identified through genome-wide gene co-expression analysis.
source: Following data pre-processing (Oldham et al., 2012), we performed genome-wide gene co-expression analysis (Lui et al., 2014; Zhang and Horvath, 2005) and identified 24 modules of co-expressed genes (termed A-X, Figure 1D; Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results with figure references.

claim: The characteristic expression pattern of each module was summarized by its first principal component, or module eigengene.
source: The characteristic expression pattern of each module was summarized by its first principal component, or module eigengene (ME) (Horvath and Dong, 2008; Oldham et al., 2008), and verified by selecting several markers among the highest ranked genes and conducting in situ hybridization (ISH) analysis.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the analytical approach with citations.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of modules based on eigengene dissimilarity revealed distinct subgroups of modules within the dendrogram.
source: Hierarchical clustering of modules based on eigengene dissimilarity revealed distinct subgroups of modules within the dendrogram (Figure 1E), suggesting broad themes of transcriptional co-variation in the incisor.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results with figure reference.

claim: Module A represents a transcriptional signature of ameloblasts.
source: This analysis immediately suggested that Module A (Figure 1E; Figure 2A) represents a transcriptional signature of ameloblasts, which are enamel-producing differentiated cells derived from epithelial stem cells in the laCL (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the interpretation with figure references.

claim: Lamb3 and Lamc2 encode subunits of Laminin 5 that are expressed by ameloblasts in developing mouse incisors.
source: For example, both Lamb3 (kME.Arank = 4) and Lamc2 (kME.Arank = 10) encode subunits of Laminin 5 that are expressed by ameloblasts in developing mouse incisors (Yoshiba et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Expression of Enam is restricted to ameloblasts.
source: Expression of Enam (kME.A rank = 11) is also restricted to ameloblasts (Kuang-Hsien Hu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Ambn and Amelx encode enamel matrix proteins that are widely used as ameloblast markers.
source: Similarly, Ambn and Amelx, which encode enamel matrix proteins that are widely used as ameloblast markers (Lee et al., 1996; Snead et al., 1988), were also strongly associated with Module A (kME.A ranks of 107 and 118, respectively; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Dact2 expression has been shown to be restricted to the dental epithelium during molar development.
source: Another gene in this module was Dact2 (kME.Arank = 192), which encodes a transcription factor-binding protein whose expression has previously been shown to be restricted to the dental epithelium during molar development (Kettunen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Module C represents a transcriptional signature of odontoblasts.
source: Further investigation showed that Module C represents a transcriptional signature of odontoblasts, which are the dentin-secreting cells comprising the outer layer of the dental pulp.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the interpretation.

claim: Bglap1 and Bglap2 are expressed by mesenchymally derived pre-odontoblasts and odontoblasts.
source: For example, Bglap1 and Bglap2 were among the top-ranked genes for Module C (Figure 2B), and these are expressed by mesenchymally derived pre-odontoblasts and odontoblasts (Bronckers et al., 1987).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support and figure reference.

claim: Phex is expressed in developing odontoblasts.
source: Phex (kME.C rank = 1) is expressed in developing odontoblasts (Ruchon et al., 1998), and Dspp, a known marker of odontoblasts (Bègue-Kirn et al., 1998; D'Souza et al., 1997), was strongly associated with Module C (kME.C rank = 190).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Dspp is a known marker of odontoblasts.
source: Phex (kME.C rank = 1) is expressed in developing odontoblasts (Ruchon et al., 1998), and Dspp, a known marker of odontoblasts (Bègue-Kirn et al., 1998; D'Souza et al., 1997), was strongly associated with Module C (kME.C rank = 190).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Kazald1 is expressed by secretory odontoblasts.
source: Similarly, Kazald1, which is expressed by secretory odontoblasts (James et al., 2004), was also associated with Module C (kME.C rank = 266).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Tmem108 shows robust and specific expression in the ameloblast lineage.
source: As shown in Figure 2C, Tmem108 (kME.A rank = 1), SOX21 (kME.A ranks = 5, 15, 1302), and StarD10 (kME.A rank = 8) all showed robust and specific expression in the ameloblast lineage.
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: SOX21 shows robust and specific expression in the ameloblast lineage.
source: As shown in Figure 2C, Tmem108 (kME.A rank = 1), SOX21 (kME.A ranks = 5, 15, 1302), and StarD10 (kME.A rank = 8) all showed robust and specific expression in the ameloblast lineage.
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: StarD10 shows robust and specific expression in the ameloblast lineage.
source: As shown in Figure 2C, Tmem108 (kME.A rank = 1), SOX21 (kME.A ranks = 5, 15, 1302), and StarD10 (kME.A rank = 8) all showed robust and specific expression in the ameloblast lineage.
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Module A consists of genes that are predominantly expressed in the ameloblast lineage of the adult mouse incisor.
source: These data demonstrate that Module A consists of genes that are predominantly expressed in the ameloblast lineage of the adult mouse incisor.
evidence: This is a direct conclusion statement based on the data.

claim: Expression of Phex is restricted to odontoblasts.
source: As expected, expression of Phex (kME.C rank = 1) was restricted to odontoblasts (Ruchon et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Expression of Sag is restricted to odontoblasts.
source: Expression of Sag (kME.C rank = 7) was also restricted to odontoblasts, while expression of Lox (kME.C rank = 8) showed a more complex pattern, with robust expression in odontoblasts but additional expression in regions where T-A cells are located in epithelium and mesenchyme (arrow and asterisk in Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Expression of Lox shows robust expression in odontoblasts but additional expression in regions where T-A cells are located in epithelium and mesenchyme.
source: Expression of Sag (kME.C rank = 7) was also restricted to odontoblasts, while expression of Lox (kME.C rank = 8) showed a more complex pattern, with robust expression in odontoblasts but additional expression in regions where T-A cells are located in epithelium and mesenchyme (arrow and asterisk in Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Module C consists of genes that are predominantly expressed in the odontoblast lineage.
source: Overall, these results indicate that Module C consists of genes that are predominantly expressed in the odontoblast lineage.
evidence: This is a direct conclusion statement based on the data.

claim: Known markers of ameloblasts possess Z.ameloblast >> Z.odontoblast.
source: We observed that known markers of ameloblasts possessed Z.ameloblast >> Z.odontoblast, and vice versa.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the distribution of expression specificity scores.

claim: The expression signatures captured by Modules A and C are both sensitive and specific.
source: These results indicate that the expression signatures captured by Modules A and C are both sensitive and specific: canonical markers of each cell type have high kME values for the appropriate module and lower kME values for the inappropriate module.
evidence: This is a direct conclusion statement based on the data.

claim: The vast majority of genes with the highest kME values for Modules A and C have not been characterized in the ameloblast or odontoblast lineages.
source: Importantly, the vast majority of genes with the highest kME values for these two modules, which are likely to play central roles in the establishment and maintenance of the functional identities of these cell types (Lui et al., 2014; Oldham et al., 2008) have not been characterized in the ameloblast or odontoblast lineages.
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Gene co-expression analysis of heterogeneous tissue samples can discern and predict transcriptional signatures of the two principal secretory cell types of the adult mouse incisor.
source: Taken together, these findings establish that gene co-expression analysis of heterogeneous tissue samples can discern and predict transcriptional signatures of the two principal secretory cell types of the adult mouse incisor.
evidence: This is a direct conclusion statement based on the findings.

claim: Module J was significantly enriched with experimentally validated markers of oligodendrocytes.
source: For example, over-representation analysis with cell type-specific gene sets revealed that Module J was significantly enriched with experimentally validated markers of oligodendrocytes (p<10−8, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–E), suggesting that this module corresponds to a transcriptional signature of Schwann cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement with statistical support and figure reference.

claim: Module J corresponds to a transcriptional signature of Schwann cells.
source: For example, over-representation analysis with cell type-specific gene sets revealed that Module J was significantly enriched with experimentally validated markers of oligodendrocytes (p<10−8, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–E), suggesting that this module corresponds to a transcriptional signature of Schwann cells.
evidence: This is a direct inference statement based on enrichment analysis.

claim: Module S was significantly enriched with experimentally validated markers of skeletal muscle cells.
source: Similarly, Module S was significantly enriched with experimentally validated markers of skeletal muscle cells (p<10−12, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement with statistical support and figure reference.

claim: Module S resulted from contamination of a small number of tissue samples by cells from the muscle tissue surrounding the jawbones.
source: It appears that this highly specific module resulted from contamination of a small number of tissue samples by cells from the muscle tissue surrounding the jawbones.
evidence: This is a direct inference statement about the source of the module.

claim: Expression of Cdkn1a, Smox, and Atp2b was detected in epithelium-forming cell types of the ameloblast, stratum intermedium, and odontoblast lineages located distal to the laCL.
source: Interestingly, expression of Cdkn1a (kME.B ranks = 2, 3, 7), Smox (kME.Branks = 4, 5, 9, 31, 68), and Atp2b (kME.B rank = 8), which were among the highest-ranked members of Module B (Supplementary file 1), was detected in epithelium-forming cell types of the ameloblast, stratum intermedium, and odontoblast lineages located distal to the laCL (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G–I).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Expression of genes contributing to Module F was detected in the distal dental pulp mesenchyme, but not in the proximal-most pulp cells.
source: Expression patterns of genes in Modules D and E were similar to those of genes contributing to Module C (data not shown), and genes contributing to Module F, including Tgfbi (kME.F ranks = 1, 2), Fgfr3 (kME.F ranks = 11, 99), and Nes1 (kME.F ranks = 28, 49), were expressed in the distal dental pulp mesenchyme, but not in the proximal-most pulp cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1J–L).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Expression of genes contributing to Modules A-F was predominantly detected in regions distal to the stem cell niches in the epithelial cervical loops and in the mesenchyme located between these epithelial regions.
source: Thus, expression of genes contributing to Modules A-F was predominantly detected in regions distal to the stem cell niches in the epithelial cervical loops and in the mesenchyme located between these epithelial regions.
evidence: This is a direct summary statement of the expression patterns.

claim: Module U was enriched for genes expressed during the mitotic phase of the cell cycle.
source: Functional enrichment analysis indicated that Module U, the second largest co-expression module, was enriched for genes expressed during the mitotic phase of the cell cycle (p=3.1×10−24).
evidence: This is a direct statement with statistical support.

claim: Expression of Pbk, Ncaph, and Cdca2 was found in actively proliferating transit-amplifying cells in the proximal incisor.
source: As predicted by the functional enrichment analysis, expression of Pbk (kME.U rank = 1), Ncaph (kME.U rank = 2), and Cdca2 (kME.U rank = 3), the three highest ranked genes contributing to Module U (Supplementary file 1), was found in actively proliferating transit-amplifying (T-A) cells in the proximal incisor (Figure 3B–D), which can be visualized as BrdU-incorporating cells using immunohistochemistry (Young et al., 1992).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data and citation support.

claim: All three genes (Pbk, Ncaph, and Cdca2) were expressed in BrdU-positive, T-A cell-containing regions in both the incisor epithelium and mesenchyme.
source: All three genes were expressed in BrdU-positive, T-A cell-containing regions in both the incisor epithelium and mesenchyme.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the expression pattern.

claim: T-A cell-specific expression was not restricted to members of Module U.
source: Interestingly, T-A cell-specific expression was not restricted to members of Module U.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the findings.

claim: Modules V, W, and X also represent T-A cell signatures.
source: We also identified a T-A cell signature in co-expression Modules V, W, and X, which were the modules most strongly positively correlated with Module U (Figure 3E–G, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I–L).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure references showing experimental data.

claim: Expression of genes in Modules V, W, and X labeled proliferating cells in both the epithelium or the mesenchyme in all cases.
source: Similar to the genes contributing to Module U, expression of genes in Modules V, W, and X labeled proliferating cells in both the epithelium or the mesenchyme in all cases.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the expression pattern.

claim: Modules N-R also represented T-A cell-specific expression signatures.
source: When we extended our follow-up analyses to modules that clustered within the same branch of the dendrogram, but that were less strongly correlated to Module U, we discovered that Modules N-R also represented T-A cell-specific expression signatures (Figure 3H–J, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure references showing experimental data.

claim: Modules T-X were enriched in genes involved in processes characteristic of the M-phase of the cell cycle.
source: Whereas Modules T-X were enriched in genes involved in processes characteristic of the M-phase of the cell cycle, Modules N-R were enriched in genes involved in biosynthetic and metabolic processes, suggesting roles during interphase, during which cell growth and DNA replication occur.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on enrichment analysis.

claim: Modules N-R were enriched in genes involved in biosynthetic and metabolic processes, suggesting roles during interphase.
source: Whereas Modules T-X were enriched in genes involved in processes characteristic of the M-phase of the cell cycle, Modules N-R were enriched in genes involved in biosynthetic and metabolic processes, suggesting roles during interphase, during which cell growth and DNA replication occur.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on enrichment analysis.

claim: T-A-specific gene co-expression modules may represent distinct biological processes that are integrated to induce or maintain proliferation.
source: Together, these data indicate that T-A-specific gene co-expression modules may represent distinct biological processes that are integrated to induce or maintain proliferation.
evidence: This is a direct inference statement based on the data.

claim: These processes may be temporally segregated in subpopulations of T-A cells.
source: They also suggest that these processes may be temporally segregated in subpopulations of T-A cells.
evidence: This is a direct inference statement based on the data.

claim: Ptch1 was associated with Module L.
source: Although Gli1 was not represented by a probe on the microarrays that we used, Ptch1, which like Gli1 reports active Hedgehog signaling and is expressed in the same pattern in the incisor as Gli1 (Seidel et al., 2010), was associated with Module L, and Sox2 was associated with Module H (Figure 4A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support and figure reference.

claim: Sox2 was associated with Module H.
source: Although Gli1 was not represented by a probe on the microarrays that we used, Ptch1, which like Gli1 reports active Hedgehog signaling and is expressed in the same pattern in the incisor as Gli1 (Seidel et al., 2010), was associated with Module L, and Sox2 was associated with Module H (Figure 4A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference.

claim: Expression of Bmi1 was detected in all specimens but not associated with a co-expression module.
source: Expression of Bmi1 was detected in all specimens but not associated with a co-expression module.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the findings.

claim: Lgr5 was not detected by the microarray in any of the samples.
source: Lgr5, another gene that recently has been suggested to be expressed by incisor stem cells (Chang et al., 2013; Suomalainen and Thesleff, 2010), was not detected by the microarray in any of the samples.
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: The limited sensitivity of microarrays for detecting low-expressed transcripts in rare cell populations in heterogeneous tissue samples may explain the lack of detection of some stem cell markers.
source: These results may reflect the limited sensitivity of microarrays for detecting low-expressed transcripts in rare cell populations in heterogeneous tissue samples.
evidence: This is a direct inference statement about the limitations of the methodology.

claim: Tbx1 was previously shown to be expressed in the epithelium of developing incisors.
source: Module H, the co-expression module with which Sox2 was most strongly associated, also contained Tbx1 (kME.Hrank = 14), which was previously shown to be expressed in the epithelium of developing incisors (Catón et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Tbx1 expression is restricted to the epithelium in the adult incisor.
source: We found that Tbx1 expression is also restricted to the epithelium in the adult incisor, and we detected transcripts in the T-A and pre-ameloblast region as well as in several cells in the proximal region of the laCL (Figure 4B) where epithelial stem cells reside.
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Expression of Epha1 was found predominantly in stellate reticulum cells in the laCL and in more distal cells subtending the SR cells adjacent to this region.
source: Expression of Epha1 was found predominantly in stellate reticulum (SR) cells in the laCL and in more distal cells subtending the SR cells adjacent to this region (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Expression of Prom2 appeared to overlap that of Tbx1 in the T-A cell and pre-ameloblast region as well as in the outer enamel epithelium of the laCL.
source: In contrast, expression of Prom2 appeared to overlap that of Tbx1 in the T-A cell and pre-ameloblast region as well as in the outer enamel epithelium (OEE) of the laCL (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Multiple genes associated strongly with two or all three modules (G, H, and I).
source: In addition to being a highly-ranked gene for Module H, Prom2 also showed a strong association to the neighboring Module I. Further investigation of Modules G and I, which were strongly positively correlated with Module H and each other (Figure 1C), revealed that multiple genes, including Epha1 and Prom2, associated strongly with two or all three modules (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference.

claim: Nkx2-3 was previously shown to be required for molar development.
source: Of the genes primarily contributing to Module G, we analyzed the expression patterns of Scnn1b (kME.G rank = 3), p63 (kME.G rank = 5), and Nkx2-3 (kME.G rank = 11), the last of which was previously shown to be required for molar development (Biben et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Scnn1b, p63, and Nkx2-3 were expressed predominantly in the T-A and OEE regions of the laCL with no or low levels of expression in the SR.
source: All three were expressed predominantly in the T-A and OEE regions of the laCL with no or low levels of expression in the SR (Figure 4D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Expression of Scnn1b, p63, and Nkx2-3 was not limited to the CL on the labial side but rather extended distally into both the OEE and differentiated ameloblasts and was also found in the liCL.
source: Expression was not limited to the CL on the labial side but rather extended distally into both the OEE and differentiated ameloblasts and was also found in the liCL.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the expression pattern.

claim: Isl1 was previously shown to be expressed exclusively in the incisor epithelium during tooth development.
source: Isl1 (kME.G rank = 33), which was previously shown to be expressed exclusively in the incisor epithelium during tooth development (Mitsiadis et al., 2003), was expressed in the same pattern in the laCL as p63, Nkx2-3, and Scnn1b, with distally extending expression maintained in the OEE and ameloblasts but decreased levels in the pre-ameloblasts (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support and figure reference.

claim: Expression of Pitx2 was detected in LRCs in the proximal SR and OEE regions.
source: Pitx2 expression appeared to be highest in the apical aspect of the laCL, where Sox2 is expressed at high levels (Juuri et al., 2012), and was also present in the SR. In the proximal SR and OEE regions, expression of Pitx2 was detected in LRCs (Figure 4H–H").
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support and figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Expression of Pitx2 was not detected in the liCL epithelium.
source: However, similar to Tbx1, Epha1 and Prom2, expression of Pitx2 was not detected in the liCL epithelium.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the expression pattern.

claim: Shh is expressed in epithelial T-A cells, pre-ameloblasts and ameloblasts in the labial incisor epithelium.
source: Shh, which is expressed in epithelial T-A cells, pre-ameloblasts and ameloblasts in the labial incisor epithelium (Seidel et al., 2010), was also among the genes contributing to Modules G, H, and I (kME.Grank = 14, kME.Hrank = 53, and kME.Irank = 7), which was surprising given the absence of Shh expression in the proximal laCL.
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: Expression of all analyzed genes contributing to Modules G, H, and I specifically overlapped with T-A cells in the epithelium and, with the exception of Shh, in the proximal laCL.
source: Thus, expression of all analyzed genes contributing to Modules G, H, and I specifically overlapped with T-A cells in the epithelium and, with the exception of Shh, in the proximal laCL.
evidence: This is a direct summary statement of the expression patterns.

claim: Modules K-M were highly correlated.
source: As with Modules G-I, Modules K-M were highly correlated, and several genes showed promiscuity for all three modules (Figure 1E, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference.

claim: Gpx3, Fbln1, and Igfbp4 are actively transcribed in the mesenchymal tissue in the proximal part of the incisor.

claim: Igfbp4 expression was observed in an additional domain in the proximal laCL epithelium.

evidence: This is a direct statement about the expression pattern.

claim: Pecam1 and Igfbp5 are expressed in LRCs in the incisor mesenchyme and laCL epithelium.

claim: Expression of genes contributing to Modules K-M was predominantly observed in cells of the periodontium.

evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Most periodontal markers identified in previous studies were associated with Modules K, L, and M.

evidence: This is a direct statement based on comparison with literature.

claim: Modules K-M may be enriched for candidate stem cell markers and genes required for periodontal tissue maintenance.
source: The expression of these markers in the proximal part of the tooth suggested that these modules may be enriched for candidate stem cell markers and genes required for periodontal tissue maintenance.
evidence: This is a direct inference statement based on the expression patterns.

claim: Igfbp5 was previously found to be increased in LRCs in the hair follicle bulge.
source: To test whether our analysis could enable functional identification of a stem cell population, we next focused on Igfbp5, which was the highest ranked gene contributing to Module K and was previously found to be increased in LRCs in the hair follicle bulge (Tumbar et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a direct statement with citation support.

claim: 24 hr after tamoxifen treatment of Igfbp5iCre-ERT2;Ai14 animals, RFP expression was detected in cells of the periodontium, the liCL and in the proximal portion and OEE of the laCL, as well as in a number of cells in the alveolar nerve.

evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Igfbp5-expressing cells supply new cells in the incisor mesenchyme surrounding the cervical loops and within the laCL and distally adjacent epithelium.
source: 14 days after treatment with tamoxifen, the number of RFP-positive cells in the incisor mesenchyme surrounding the cervical loops and within the laCL and distally adjacent epithelium was strongly increased when compared to 24 hr post-induction, suggesting that the originally labeled Igfbp5-expressing cells supply new cells in these regions (Figure 4M).
evidence: This is a direct inference statement based on lineage tracing data.

claim: RFP-positive cells were absent from the inner dental pulp mesenchyme and remained restricted to the periodontal portion of the incisor mesenchyme 1 month after tamoxifen treatment.

claim: Igfbp5-expressing cells contribute to epithelial and periodontium homeostasis without contributing to maintenance of the pulp compartment.
source: These findings suggest that Igfbp5-expressing cells contribute to epithelial and periodontium homeostasis without contributing to maintenance of the pulp compartment.
evidence: This is a direct inference statement based on lineage tracing data.

claim: Lrig1 is a marker of stem cells in the intestine and the skin.

claim: Lrig1 was expressed in the proximal incisor mesenchyme and laCL epithelium but not in pulp cells, odontoblasts or differentiated epithelial cells.
source: Consistent with this observation, Lrig1 was expressed in the proximal incisor mesenchyme and laCL epithelium but not in pulp cells, odontoblasts or differentiated epithelial cells (Figure 4G).

claim: Expression of the Lrig1Cre-ERT2 allele was restricted to regions in the incisor where Lrig1 mRNA is expressed and included some, but not all, BrdU-LRCs.

evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Lrig1 is more restricted in the SR and absent from the most apical portion of the Gli1lacZ-positive domain of the laCL.
source: We found that Lrig1 expression, as reflected by CreER-mediated RFP expression 24 hr after tamoxifen administration, largely overlaps with Gli1 in Lrig1Cre-ERT2/+;R26RFP/+;Gli1lacZ/+mice; however, Lrig1 is more restricted in the SR and absent from the most apical portion of the Gli1lacZ-positive domain of the laCL (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: The number of RFP-positive cells in the proximal incisor mesenchyme strongly increased 14 days after induction with tamoxifen.

claim: Lrig1-positive cells in the mesenchyme turn over more rapidly when compared to epithelial cells that express Lrig1.

claim: RFP-positive cells were absent from the mesenchyme of the dental pulp but were restricted to the periodontal tissue surrounding the epithelial cervical loops on the outer surface of the incisor.

claim: Lrig1 marks two distinct pools of stem cells, one in the incisor epithelium that enables renewal of epithelial cell types, and one in the proximal mesenchyme that produces cells contributing to the periodontium.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that Lrig1 marks two distinct pools of stem cells, one in the incisor epithelium that enables renewal of epithelial cell types, such as ameloblasts, and one in the proximal mesenchyme that produces cells contributing to the periodontium.

claim: The periodontal mesenchyme in the incisor is maintained by a mesenchymal stem cell pool that is separate from the progenitors that maintain the mesenchymal cells of the dental pulp.

claim: Acta2 had high rankings for Module L based on data from three different microarray probes.

claim: In molars, lineage tracing has shown that Acta2 is expressed by periodontal progenitors.

evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: Acta2 is expressed by periodontal progenitors in the incisor.

evidence: This is a direct conclusion statement based on lineage tracing data.

claim: The progeny of Lrig1-positive cells labeled three months prior to analysis did not contribute to all regions of the periodontal mesenchyme marked by ACTA2.
source: Interestingly, the progeny of Lrig1-positive cells that were labeled three months prior to analysis did not contribute to all regions of the periodontal mesenchyme marked by ACTA2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3H).
evidence: This is a direct statement with figure reference showing experimental data.

claim: RFP-positive cells from Lrig1 lineage tracing were absent from the outermost layer of periodontal tissue, close to the bone.

claim: Subpopulations of periodontal progenitors, marked by Lrig1 and Acta2 expression, promote renewal of distinct regions of periodontal tissues during incisor homeostasis.

claim: Different cell types will have different signal to noise ratios in gene co-expression analysis.
